zh.question: 消息不是纸飞机，也没有连着两部手机的电线，它靠谁到达远方？
zh.observe: 先逐步追踪编号 1。依次关掉本机接入、中间路径和对方接入，比较部分停在哪里；恢复连接后继续。移动本机时看下一个未发出的编号换到 A 还是 B，最后把送达与模拟打开分开。

academic.title: 无线接入后还有基础设施
academic.body: 基站收发无线电信号，把手机接入移动通信网络。天线可装在塔上、建筑上或较小站点。接入网络与后续网络不是同一段：回程可以使用光纤、电缆或无线链路，本图选择有线代表路线。家庭 Wi‑Fi 则先经过本地接入点，再进入家庭网络及互联网；接上本地接入点并不保证互联网服务可达。

academic.title: 编号是追踪信息的办法，不是飞行物
academic.body: 消息先表示为数字信息。图中三份只帮助读者追踪与拼接，不对应真实文本长度或固定协议格式。网络设备依照地址转发数据；通信栈中的分段、顺序恢复和应用消息拼接有不同责任。以 TCP 为例，它能向应用提供可靠的有序字节流，但并不自动代表收件人读过内容。其他传输协议和应用确认规则不同。

academic.title: 网络路径、等待和确认各有边界
academic.body: 图中“网络与服务”是对多个网络及可能的消息服务的合并表示；并非所有通信都经过同一台服务器。SMS、联网聊天、通话及不同应用的路径和确认方式可能不同。模型中关闭某段只会阻塞该段尚未完成的传送，保留已走过的部分；恢复后可继续。实际网络可能重传、绕路、暂存或失败，本图不计算这些协议、无线强度或真实时延。图中送达由俯看两端的观察者统计，不模拟返回给发送方的确认消息。

zh.misconception: 手机通常不是直接把聊天内容无线送到另一部远方手机；“无线”描述其中的接入段，不代表整条路线都没有电缆。
zh.boundary: 这是本地的代表性联网聊天示意，不发真实消息。三枚编号、六段路线、先后顺序和步数用于教学，时间、尺寸和距离未标定；中间路径无备用路线。未模拟丢包、重传、切换信令或加密，不能据图判断隐私安全。

narration.label: 远方的屏幕为什么会亮
narration.text: 我们想把“公园见”告诉远方的朋友。手机不能把声音喊得那么远，也没有一根线直接连着朋友的手机。它把消息表示成数字信息，交给身边的连接，再沿着网络走。画里把信息分成三个带编号的部分，方便我们追踪。它们不是三颗真的会飞的小球。
narration.cue: 从三个本机编号开始，指出两端手机与中间基站。

narration.label: 天线后面还有一条路
narration.text: 先跟着第一个编号走。手机用看不见的无线电信号连接基站。看，到了基站还没到朋友那里呢！基站连着更大的网络。我们这幅图用绿色线表示电缆和光纤，再经过网络与消息服务，进入朋友那边的网络。设备帮助信息找到下一段路，文字不会自己认路。
narration.cue: 逐步推进编号 1，比较无线接入的金色虚线和有线网络的绿色线。

narration.label: 断掉一段会怎样
narration.text: 假如朋友的手机暂时没有连接，最后一段就过不去。信息在图中等待，收件区还没有拼齐，不能说已经送到了。现在把连接恢复，再让旅程继续。你也可以比较本机离线和中间路径不通，它们会停在不同地方。真实服务有时能等一等，有时也会告诉你发送失败。
narration.cue: 重置后关闭对方连接，推进到第五步；恢复后继续。再单独比较本机与网络断点。

narration.label: 送到了，也要等人打开
narration.text: 三个编号都到了，手机能把整条消息显示出来。不过手机收到，不等于朋友已经看过。对方打开消息是另一件事。在真实生活里，不同应用的记号可能不同。发消息前，可以请大人一起确认收件人；住址、密码和私人照片不要发给陌生人。图里的小实验不需要你填任何私人消息。
narration.cue: 推进到十八步，先观察送达状态，再模拟对方打开；最后比较已读与未读。

en.question: A message is not a paper plane, and no wire joins the two phones directly. What helps it travel far away?
en.observe: Track part 1 one step at a time. Disable the sender’s access, the middle path and the recipient’s access separately; compare where the part waits, then reconnect and continue. Move the sender and see whether the next unsent part uses A or B. Keep delivery separate from simulated opening.

academic.title: Infrastructure follows the radio link
academic.body: A base station sends and receives radio signals to connect a phone to a mobile network. Antennas may be on towers, buildings or smaller sites. Access and onward transport are distinct links. Backhaul can use fibre, cables or wireless connections; this diagram chooses a wired example. Home Wi-Fi first reaches a local access point, then the home network and Internet. A local connection does not guarantee that an Internet service is reachable.

academic.title: Numbers track information, not flying objects
academic.body: A message is represented as digital information. Three parts make tracking and assembly visible; they do not correspond to text length or a fixed protocol format. Network equipment forwards using addresses. Segmentation, restoring order and assembling an application message have different responsibilities in the communication stack. TCP, for example, provides an ordered, reliable byte stream to an application. That does not confirm that a person has read the message. Other protocols and application confirmations differ.

academic.title: Routes, waiting and confirmation have limits
academic.body: “Networks and service” groups several networks and a possible messaging service. Not all communication passes through one server. SMS, online chat, calls and different apps may follow different paths and confirmation rules. An unavailable link blocks only an unfinished crossing in this model, keeping completed parts in place; reconnecting permits continuation. Real networks may retransmit, reroute, store or fail. Protocols, radio strength and real delays are not calculated here. Delivery is counted by an observer of both ends; returned confirmations to the sender are not modelled.

en.misconception: A phone usually does not send chat content directly by radio to a distant phone. Wireless describes an access link, not a guarantee that the whole route has no cables.
en.boundary: This is a local representative online-chat diagram, sending no real message. Three numbers, six links, ordering and step counts are teaching choices. Time, sizes and distances are uncalibrated; there is no alternate middle route. Loss, retransmission, handover signalling and encryption are not modelled. The drawing cannot establish privacy or security.

narration.label: Why a distant screen lights up
narration.text: We want to tell a friend far away, “See you at the park!” A phone cannot shout that far, and no wire directly joins it to the friend’s phone. It represents the message as digital information, reaches a nearby connection and travels through networks. Our picture uses three numbered parts so we can follow them. They are not three little balls that really fly through the air.
narration.cue: Begin with all three numbers on the sender, pointing out both phones and the base stations.

narration.label: An antenna has an onward link
narration.text: Follow the first number. The phone uses invisible radio signals to connect to a base station. Reaching the station does not mean reaching the friend! The station connects to a larger network. Our green lines represent cables and fibre, continuing through networks and a messaging service into the friend’s network. Equipment forwards information along the next link. Words do not find their own way.
narration.cue: Step part 1 along the route, comparing the gold radio dashes and green wired links.

narration.label: What if one link is unavailable
narration.text: If the friend’s phone is not connected, the last link cannot finish. A part waits in our picture, and the inbox is incomplete. We cannot say the message is delivered yet. Reconnect and continue. Compare a sender without access and an unavailable middle path: parts wait in different places. Real services sometimes wait, and sometimes report that sending failed.
narration.cue: Reset, disable recipient access and reach step five. Reconnect. Compare the sender and middle-network blocks separately.

narration.label: Delivery is different from reading
narration.text: All three numbers arrive, and the phone can show the whole message. Receiving it does not mean the friend has read it. Opening it is a separate event. Real apps can use different signs. Before sending a real message, check the recipient with an adult. Do not send strangers your address, passwords or private photos. This little experiment needs no personal message from you.
narration.cue: Reach step eighteen, compare delivery before and after simulating the recipient opening it.
